correctness.rationale: For every full-dimensional type-B deformation, Minkowski averaging preserves the normal-fan coarsening and cannot decrease the inradius or increase the circumradius. Weyl-invariant deformations are signed-permutation orbit polytopes. Established signed-majorization facet inequalities imply r=min_k B_k/sqrt(k); orbit vertex barycenter zero gives R=norm(b). After r=1, B_k>=sqrt(k); summation by parts with decreasing positive d_k-d_(k+1) yields dot(d,b)>=norm(d)^2. Cauchy forces norm(b)>=norm(d), equality exactly b=d. Strictly decreasing d ensures 3^n-1 genuine tangent facets. The asymptotic follows from d_k^2=1/(4k)+O(k^-2). The finite checker corroborates n=2..5 and representative dimensions 2..127, not replacing proof.

value.rationale: The sharp optimum is over the full infinite-dimensional family of nonsymmetric Coxeter fan deformations in each ambient n, a natural constrained sphere-approximation problem. A uniquely prescribed symmetric extremizer simultaneously makes all 3^n−1 facets tangent, and its best radius quotient has a surprising logarithmic, not algebraic, decay. The optimization and equality theory are not simply fixed-object facet calculations or arbitrary numerical slices.
